governing_question: Do the people governed by an election retain meaningful influence over that election's political economy?
not_the_question: Must every dollar literally originate inside a candidate's district?
instrumentation_note: OpenFEC federal races are the instrumentation pilot. The destination universe is Arkansas statewide → legislative → county → municipal → school board.

outside_money_taxonomy.rule: These phenomena are not interchangeable. Do not collapse them into a single 'outside money' claim.

phenomena.name: individual_receipts_outside_constituency
phenomena.definition: Itemized individual contributions to a candidate committee whose disclosed contributor geography is outside the race constituency (state for statewide/Senate; district/state rules for House as locked).
phenomena.probe_evidence: schedule_a/by_state AR vs non-AR shares on principal committees

phenomena.name: pac_committee_money
phenomena.definition: Receipts from other political committees (PACs) reported on candidate totals.
phenomena.probe_evidence: candidates/totals other_political_committee_contributions (stored as pac_contributions in probe)

phenomena.name: party_money
phenomena.definition: Receipts from party committees reported on candidate totals.
phenomena.probe_evidence: OpenFEC candidates/totals political_party_committee_contributions field exists; not separately stored in locality probe v1 — pull on measure-lock enrich

phenomena.name: independent_expenditures
phenomena.definition: Schedule E spending supporting/opposing a candidate by committees other than the candidate's authorized committee.

phenomena.name: organizational_intermediary_funding
phenomena.definition: Funds routed through nonprofits, conduits, joint fundraising, or layered committees before appearing as a contributor or spender.
phenomena.probe_evidence: Visible only when intermediary itself is the disclosed contributor/spender; layers behind often opaque

phenomena.name: untraceable_beneficial_source_funding
phenomena.definition: Material election spending whose significant original human/organizational funders cannot be identified from public disclosure.
phenomena.probe_evidence: Chain break after spender committee on Schedule E; dark-money patterns

proposed_measures.name: local_dollar_share
proposed_measures.definition_draft: Share of itemized individual receipts from contributors inside a locked constituency geography.
proposed_measures.constituency_lock_needed: state for Senate; district vs state rule for House must be frozen before publication use

proposed_measures.name: in_state_out_of_state_share
proposed_measures.definition_draft: AR vs non-AR share of itemized contributor-state dollars to principal committee.

proposed_measures.name: small_dollar_participation
proposed_measures.definition_draft: Share of Schedule A by_size size=200 ($200 and under) relative to sized totals; not unique donor headcount.

proposed_measures.name: donor_concentration
proposed_measures.definition_draft: Concentration among itemized individual/PAC contributors; disclosure only.

proposed_measures.name: independent_spending_ratio
proposed_measures.definition_draft: Schedule E total (support+oppose) relative to candidate committee receipts or disbursements (denominator lock required).

proposed_measures.name: beneficial_source_observability
proposed_measures.definition_draft: Ordinal score of how far the disclosure chain can be walked: spender known / intermediary known / original sources known.
proposed_measures.finding: Impossibility of full beneficial-source observability under current federal disclosure is itself an important research result for HYP-125 Track A/B.

hard_distinctions: PAC/committee money ≠ independent expenditure ≠ party money ≠ untraceable beneficial-source funding
